skill.name: buyer-question
skill.description: Define one buyer question, one content brief, and one kill date before developing the next page.
skill.summary: A focused workflow for turning buyer language into a testable content brief.
skill.author: cmj-hub

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a documentation command shown in SKILL.md, not executable code. It is a false positive because the skill instructs the user to run a local scoring script and provides no executable implementation or untrusted command construction. No semantic security findings were identified.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks contain a documentation example for a user-run Python scoring command in SKILL.md. The skill contains no executable code and does not construct or invoke commands with untrusted input.

content.value_statement: Turn vague content ideas into one buyer-focused question, a concise brief, and a clear kill date. Use the workflow to test real search intent before expanding the topic.
actual_capabilities: Express a content idea as one question in the buyer's own words.
Create one focused brief for the next page.
Set a kill date for stopping or revisiting the idea.
Identify when a topic has become a keyword list instead of a buyer question.
Provide a checklist for reviewing the question and brief.
limitations: It does not perform keyword research or retrieve search volume.
It does not write the complete page or content campaign.
It does not verify buyer demand with external analytics.
It does not replace editorial judgment about the kill date.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Content Idea
use_cases.description: Turn an early topic idea into one buyer question, one brief, and one decision date.

use_cases.title: Validate a Search Topic
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed page answers a clear question instead of targeting an unfocused keyword list.

use_cases.title: Align a Writing Assignment
use_cases.description: Give a writer a narrow question, a defined brief, and a review point before drafting begins.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a Buyer Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this topic as one question a buyer would type: [topic]. Use the buyer's words.

prompt_templates.title: Create the Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: For this buyer question, write one focused brief and propose a practical kill date: [question].

prompt_templates.title: Check Search Intent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft topic. Identify the buyer question, remove keyword-list language, and state the page brief: [topic].

prompt_templates.title: Run the Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the workflow to [idea]. Return one buyer question, one brief, one kill date, and a final review decision.

output_examples.input: Topic: onboarding emails for a small SaaS product.
output_examples.output: Buyer question: How do I write onboarding emails that help new SaaS users reach their first success?

output_examples.input: Question: How can a small team plan onboarding emails? Create the brief and kill date.
output: Brief: Explain a short onboarding sequence with one purpose for each email.
Kill date: Review the topic after two weeks and stop if the question remains too broad.

output_examples.input: Topic: analytics, dashboards, metrics, reporting, and KPIs.
output_examples.output: Review: This is a keyword list. Narrow it to one buyer question before creating a brief.

best_practices: Write the question in the buyer's own words.
Keep one question paired with one brief and one kill date.
Review the idea again when the kill date arrives.
anti_patterns: Do not replace the buyer question with a list of keywords.
Do not create a calendar of topics when one focused page is needed.
Do not skip the kill date and continue an unproven idea indefinitely.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces one buyer question, one content brief, and one kill date.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Content strategists, SEO specialists, and editors can use it during early page planning.

faq.question: Does it perform keyword research?
faq.answer: No. It helps focus the question, but it does not retrieve search data or volume.

faq.question: What is a kill date?
faq.answer: A kill date is the planned point for reviewing, stopping, or revising an idea.

faq.question: Can it create a complete article?
faq.answer: No. It defines the question and brief before drafting begins.

faq.question: How do I avoid an unfocused topic?
faq.answer: Rewrite the topic as one buyer question and remove extra keywords or separate goals.
